test.title: SV-11524 - Work orders of a deleted lead sit under Deleted technician, which takes no drops
test.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role: {Technician-A} and {Technician-B}. {Technician-A} was made for this case only and has no labor on any work order, because this test deletes that staff record.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614711 Dana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C614711 Eli.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A}, and {Work-order-2} with no lead technician. {Technician-B} is not the technician on any line of {Work-order-1}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614711 Deleted Lead, and {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S10043-17901 and S10043-17902.
  • Starting screen: your initials (top right) > "Settings" > "Staff", in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
test.custom_steps:
1. Click the pencil icon on {Technician-A}.
  2. Click "Delete" and confirm.
  3. Go to "Work Orders" > "All" > "Board View".
  4. Type the name of {Customer-A} in "Search".
  5. Read the header of the column that holds the card for {Work-order-1}.
  6. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} from "Unassigned" onto that column and let go.
  7. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  8. Click "List" in the display switcher.
  9. Click "Board View" in the display switcher.
  10. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the staff record of {Technician-A} opens.
  • Step 2: {Technician-A} is no longer in the "Staff" list.
  • Step 3: Board View shows.
  • Step 4: the cards for {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} show.
  • Step 5: the header reads "Deleted technician", shows the inactive marker and has no drag grip.
  • Step 6: the drop is refused: the card for {Work-order-2} stays in "Unassigned".
  • Step 7: {Work-order-1} sits in a group headed "Deleted technician" with the inactive marker.
  • Step 8: in the row for {Work-order-1} the "Lead Technician" cell reads "Unassigned", as List shows today.
  • Step 9: Board View shows again.
  • Step 10: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with an "Undo" button.

Step 8 expects "Unassigned": PRD version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling) changed S3-R20e to say so (it said "blank, as today"), as the QA lead decided on 19 Oct 2026.

Known problem (SV-11416, open: https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11416): today, at step 5, the column reads "Unknown Technician" with a generic person icon, no inactive marker and a drag grip, and the deleted technician's name is not shown.

1. If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new.

2. If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it.

3. If it passes, the fix has shipped: tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S3-R20e, S4-N5, S3-N4, S2-N3 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. Defect SV-11416 (open). Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

SV-11416 asked the product owner what happens when a lead technician is deleted; the spec covered only a deactivated lead. PRD version 59 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling on Slavcho Mitrov's question on SV-11416) added S3-R20e: such work orders sit under "Deleted technician" with the inactive marker and no grip, take no drops, can be dragged out, and List shows the lead blank (version 68 changed this to "Unassigned"). In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the message after a lead change became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo (step 10). This case follows version 59 and later (was: no "Unknown Technician" column, the header naming the technician as List does).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R20e: “Work orders whose lead technician was deleted in Settings → Staff (the name no longer exists) sit in one column on Board View and one group in Tech View labeled “Deleted technician”, with the inactive marker and no drag grip. Work orders can be dragged out of it; nothing can be dropped onto it. List shows “Unassigned” in the Lead Technician column for these work orders, as today.”
  • S4-N5: “Nothing can be dropped onto the column/group of an inactive technician (S2-N2, S3-N2) or of a technician who is not enrolled at this location (S3-R20c).”
  • S3-N4: “Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.”
  • S2-N3: “Indicate deactivated technicians as inactive in group headers.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11416)

test.title: SV-11545 - Invoiced and Paid work orders show why the lead can't be changed
test.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 25 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • [Tech-A]: one eligible technician at this location. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • [Tech-B]: a second eligible technician at this location (same rules as [Tech-A]). Their column shows on Board View and their group in Tech View even with no work orders, so the locked work orders can be dragged over it.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" (used by this case only), with a contact, and two work orders with Lead Technician [Tech-A] set before invoicing: [WO-1] Invoiced and [WO-2] Paid.
  • Names and numbers are examples; what must hold: one Invoiced and one Paid work order, both with a lead.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard) and [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. How to reach each status (standard steps): Estimate = a new work order whose lines are not approved. Approved = approve its lines. In Progress = a technician clicks Start time clock on an approved line's Labor row. Review = set the work order to Ready for Review with its status control. Complete = enter a tech story on every line, complete each line, then complete the work order. Invoiced = Finance tab > Create Invoice (the work order needs a contact person). Paid = record a full payment on that invoice. Declined = decline the estimate.
  6. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Assign lead technician > click the technician; it is assigned at once.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-511): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Invoiced.
    • [WO-2] (e.g. S1-366): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Paid.
  7. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" shows [WO-1] (Invoiced) and [WO-2] (Paid), both led by [Tech-A]. If not, fix the status or lead before starting; then clear the search.
test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" in Search.
  3. Look at the [WO-1] card and write down any sign that it can only be reordered within its technician (e.g. a lock icon).
  4. Hover the lock icon on the [WO-1] card and read its tooltip.
  5. Hover the card, click More actions and hover the Reassign lead technician action.
  6. Read the tooltip shown next to the Reassign lead technician action.
  7. Hover the Unassign action and read its tooltip.
  8. Press Escape to close the menu.
  9. Drag the [WO-1] card over [Tech-B]'s column and, without releasing it, read the note at the top of [Tech-B]'s column.
  10. Release the card and read which column it is in.
  11. Repeat steps 3 to 10 for [WO-2].
  12. Repeat steps 3 to 11 in Tech View on the rows, dragging each row over [Tech-B]'s group.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Invoiced and Paid cards and rows carry a lock icon, the visible sign that they can only be reordered within their current technician and not moved to another one.
  • Hovering the lock icon shows the tooltip “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-1] and “Paid · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-2].
  • Reassign lead technician and Unassign are shown disabled, and their tooltip reads exactly: Invoiced · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-1]) or Paid · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-2]). (A straight or curly apostrophe is not a difference.)
  • While [WO-1] or [WO-2] is dragged over [Tech-B]'s column or group, the note at its top reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-1]) or “Paid · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-2]).
  • On release the drop is refused: the card or row stays with [Tech-A], and its lead stays [Tech-A].

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-N6, S4-N7 and S4-N2, read 19 Oct 2026. PRD §9 User Feedback Summary row "Reassignment not allowed in current status". Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): lock icon next to the number with tooltip "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" and a locked menu note; since PRD version 68 the PRD uses the same words, and the PRD text is asserted here. Source-verified 19 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that an Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Invoiced or Paid status. An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

AUTOMATION: READY

  • Step 2: a card shows the focus ring.
  • Step 3: the card for {Work-order-1} shows the focus ring.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) Phase 11. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 28, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Until 15 Oct 2026 Story 11 only listed keyboard behaviour the design still had to define, so this case asked the tester to try keys and write down what each did. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 28): Tab reaches every control, Enter opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the control that opened a menu or dialog, reassigning by keyboard goes through the ⋯ menu, and there is no keyboard drag. PRD version 54 rewrites Story 11 into these requirements, and this case now checks them.

Chris Ward's answer 28 (15 Oct 2026) and PRD version 54 said Tab reaches every row, card and header in on-screen order. PRD versions 55, 60 and 61 (15 and 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and the QA triage of SV-11395, SV-11397, SV-11422 and SV-11421) changed this: each view is one Tab stop that lands on a work order, and the arrow keys move between cards, rows, headers and columns. PRD version 62 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward) added where the first Tab lands when nothing has been focused yet (the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first one when Unassigned is collapsed or empty); the steps are unchanged. This case follows version 68, the latest.

  • S11-R9: “Assigning, reassigning and unassigning by keyboard go through the more-actions menu: Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician (S3-R14) opens the lead technician dialog, and Unassign is a menu item. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”
  • S4-N1: “Require Work Orders create and edit permission to drag work orders or use Assign lead technician, Reassign lead technician or Unassign. A user without it who drags a card or row over another technician’s column or group sees the design’s note “You don’t have permission to assign technicians” at the top of that column or group, and the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or, when none has been, the first work order shown in on-screen order: the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first row or card when Unassigned is collapsed or empty (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • Tech plan Phase 11 tests: “a keyboard-initiated reassign is refused for a locked status and without permission (S11-N1).”

test.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on: {Technician-A} and {Technician-B}.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C97022 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two Approved work orders, {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}, both led by {Technician-A}. Neither has a shift on the Schedule, and {Technician-B} is not the technician on any of their lines.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept 92916, with work orders S2-37664 and S2-37665.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
test.custom_steps:
1. Click once in "Search", then press Tab until a card in {Technician-A}'s column shows a blue focus ring.
  2. Press Tab.
  3. Press Enter.
  4. Press Escape.
  5. Press Enter, choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  6. Press Escape.
  7. With the mouse, click "Technician" in the filter bar, tick {Technician-A} and press Escape.
  8. Click once in "Search", then press Tab until the top card in {Technician-A}'s column shows a blue focus ring.
  9. Press Tab, press Enter, choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  10. In the window, choose {Technician-B} with the keyboard and confirm with the keyboard.
  11. Press Tab, press Enter, choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  12. In the window, choose {Technician-B} with the keyboard and confirm with the keyboard.
  13. Press Enter.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: one of the two cards in {Technician-A}'s column has a blue focus ring.
  • Step 2: that card's "More actions" (…) button shows and has the focus ring.
  • Step 3: the "More actions" menu opens and offers "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 4: the menu closes, nothing changes, and the focus ring is back on the "More actions" button.
  • Step 5: the "Reassign lead technician" window opens.
  • Step 6: the window closes, the card still has {Technician-A} as its lead, and the focus ring is back on the "More actions" button.
  • Step 7: only {Technician-A}'s column shows, holding both {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}. Every other column is hidden.
  • Step 8: the top card in {Technician-A}'s column has the focus ring.
  • Step 9: the "Reassign lead technician" window opens for that work order.
  • Step 10: the window closes and the card leaves {Technician-A}'s column (it no longer matches the Technician filter). The focus ring moves to the other card, the one left in {Technician-A}'s column, and can be seen.
  • Step 11: the "Reassign lead technician" window opens for the last work order.
  • Step 12: the window closes and the last card leaves. The board is replaced by "No work orders match these filters", then "Try removing a filter to widen your results.", with a "Clear all filters" button. The "Clear all filters" button has the focus ring.
  • Step 13: the filters are cleared, including the Technician filter, and the board shows the technicians' columns again. {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are both in {Technician-B}'s column.

Known problem (SV-11582, Open; Bilal Muzamil, staging build v26.40.20-0509710, 20 Oct 2026): at step 12 "No work orders match these filters" shows, but no focus ring is anywhere: the arrow keys do nothing and the next Tab jumps back to the top of the page. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, report it. (3) If the "Clear all filters" button has the focus ring and step 13 works, mark it Passed and tell the QA lead: the fix has shipped.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, stories SV-10054 (Story 11, Keyboard access and focus), SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options), SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View) and SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); ticket SV-11582

  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or, when none has been, the first work order shown in on-screen order: the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first row or card when Unassigned is collapsed or empty (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R2: “Every control a mouse can use in Tech View and Board View is reachable with Tab and works with Enter or Space, as the design system’s menus and dialogs do: the more-actions button (which appears on keyboard focus, S3-R13), the Columns options, the x on a filter chip, and the display switcher. Technician names behind avatars show on keyboard focus, the same as on hover.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • S3-R14: “Include the lead technician action in the card’s more-actions menu: “Assign lead technician” on a work order with no lead technician, “Reassign lead technician” on one that has a lead technician.”
  • S11-R9: “Assigning, reassigning and unassigning by keyboard go through the more-actions menu: Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician (S3-R14) opens the lead technician dialog, and Unassign is a menu item. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”
  • S4-R4: “The card or row more-actions menu opens the lead technician dialog, titled “Assign lead technician” or “Reassign lead technician” to match the menu item it was opened from (S3-R14).”
  • S11-R5: “Escape closes an open menu, dialog or tooltip without changing anything.”
  • S11-R6: “When a menu or dialog closes, focus returns to the control that opened it.”
  • S1-R15: “Choosing one or more shows only those technicians’ groups or columns; every other group or column, pinned ones included, is hidden.”
  • S11-E1: “When the focused work order leaves the result (for example after a filter change or a reassignment), focus moves to the next row or card in the same group or column, or to that group or column header when none is left. When the move leaves nothing matching the filters, so the board or table is replaced by the “No work orders match these filters” empty state (S1-N1a), for example moving the last work order of the only technician chosen in the Technician filter, focus moves to its Clear all filters button.”
  • S1-N1a: “With filters active, with or without a search, the empty state reads “No work orders match these filters”, then “Try removing a filter to widen your results.”, with a Clear all filters button.”
  • S1-R15a: “The Technician filter combines with every other filter and with Assigned to me: a work order shows only if it matches all of them. When nothing matches, the empty state of S1-N1a applies, and Clear all filters also clears the Technician filter.”

test.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and See financial data, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is 1440 px wide, with the browser zoom at 100%.
  • The design pictures DC-12-board-card-hover-button-light-1440.png, DC-12-board-card-menu-light-1440.png and DC-12-tech-row-menu-locked-light-1440.png are open beside the app at 100% zoom (actual size); they are attached to this case.
  • In the design pictures the names, numbers, dates and amounts are sample data, and the rank numbers (1, 2, 3 …) beside rows and cards are left out of this release, so do not compare those.
  • The design's menu words read "Reassign Lead Tech" and "Unassign"; the case follows the PRD's words, so compare only the look and the place of the button and the menu. The design's locked note "Invoiced · can't be reassigned" is the PRD's tooltip too.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC12 Rae Menu) is an active technician at {Location-A}.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST DC12 More Actions") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17834) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
  • Work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17835) for {Customer-A} is Invoiced and led by {Technician-A}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter (if the Asset on Site chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off, Search is empty and density is Regular (the default).
test.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Look at {Work-order-1}'s card without hovering it.
  3. Hover {Work-order-1}'s card.
  4. Click the three-dot button that appears.
  5. Press Escape.
  6. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  7. Hover {Work-order-1}'s row.
  8. Click the three-dot button at the right end of the row.
  9. Press Escape.
  10. Hover {Work-order-2}'s row and click its three-dot button.
  11. Hover the greyed-out Reassign lead technician item.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: no three-dot button shows on the card.
  • Step 3: the card's border darkens and a soft shadow appears, and a small white square button with three dots appears at the card's top right, over the right end of the status pill, as in the hover design picture.
  • Step 4: a white menu opens below the button, lined up with the button's right edge, with Reassign lead technician as its first item and an outline icon before each item, as in the menu design picture.
  • Step 7: the row turns light grey and a three-dot button appears at the right end of the row.
  • Step 8: the same kind of white menu opens below the button, lined up with its right edge.
  • Step 10: the menu's Reassign lead technician item is greyed out and cannot be chosen, as in the locked-menu design picture, and Unassign is greyed out too.
  • Step 11: the tooltip reads "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned".

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View), SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S3-R13, S3-R14, S4-R4 and S4-N6, read 19 Oct 2026; Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html", states states__work-orders__board-card-menu-button-over-badge__light__1440, states__work-orders__board-card-menu__light__1440 and states__work-orders__tech-row-menu-locked__light__1440 (design pictures DC-12-board-card-hover-button-light-1440.png, DC-12-board-card-menu-light-1440.png, DC-12-tech-row-menu-locked-light-1440.png, rendered from that export at the width in the name), read 14 Oct 2026. Where the PRD says nothing about the look, the design is the source. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Ahtasham Amjad asked Chris Ward on 14 Oct 2026 whether More actions may cover part of the status pill (the design does not show the keyboard-focus state); until he answers, no result is set for how much of the pill the button covers. The design's menu words differ from the PRD's; this case follows the PRD. Since PRD version 68 the locked tooltip is the design's words, “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned”.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R13: “Reveal the card’s more-actions overlay on hover or keyboard focus.”
  • S3-R14: “Include the lead technician action in the card’s more-actions menu: “Assign lead technician” on a work order with no lead technician, “Reassign lead technician” on one that has a lead technician.”
  • S4-R4: “The card or row more-actions menu opens the lead technician dialog, titled “Assign lead technician” or “Reassign lead technician” to match the menu item it was opened from (S3-R14).”
  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, more-actions menu: “transform: translateX(-100%); width: 216px; padding: 4px; border-radius: var(--sv-radius-md); background: var(--sv-surface);”
